entries.topic_title: Subject Pronouns + To be Present (Positive) - Rule
entries.nuer: In Nuer, the present-tense “to be” is not expressed with a verb; instead, the subject pronoun alone carries the meaning of “am/is/are,” using Ɛ for singular subjects (Ɛ Ɣän, Ɛ ji̱n, Ɛ jɛn) and Kɛ for plural subjects (Kɛ kɔn, Kɛ yiɛn, Kɛ kɛn).
entries.english: In English Language, the “be” form “am” is used for the subject pronoun I, “are” is used for the subject pronouns We/You/They and “is” is used for the subject pronouns He/She/it.

entries.topic_title: Present Continuous Tense - Affirmative Form - Rule
entries.nuer: In Nuer Language, the present continuous tense is formed by changing the verb ending according to the subject: For first-person singular (I), the verb ends in “ä” For second-person singular (you – male or female), the verb ends in “i̱” For third-person singular (he/she), the verb ends in “ɛ” For first-person plural (we), second-person plural (you all), and third-person plural (they), the verb form remains unchanged
entries.english: In English Language, “Present participle form” of a verb is used irrespective of person, number, and gender but to indicate present continuous tense, helping verb “am” is used for the subject I, “are” for We/You/They and “is” for He/She/It.

entries.topic_title: Past Continuous Tense - Interrogative form - Rule
entries.nuer: In Nuer language, there are no interrogative words like in English to make interrogative statement. However, intonation in spoken language and punctuation mark “?” in written language indicate interrogative form. The “verb form” varies with respective person, number, and gender. The verb form begins and ends as mentioned in the below table.
entries.english: In English Language, “Present participle form” of a verb is used irrespective of person, number, and gender but to indicate past continuous tense, helping verb “was” is used for the subject I/He/She and “were” for We/You/They.

entries.topic_title: Past Continuous Tense - Negative Form - Rule
entries.nuer: In the Nuer language, the negative marker in the past tense changes according to the subject: For first-person singular (I), the negative marker is "/ka̱n". For second-person singular (you – male and female), the negative marker is "/käni̱". For third-person singular (he/she), the negative marker is "/känɛ".For all plural forms (we, you plural, they), the negative marker is "/kän".
entries.english: In English Language, “Present participle form” of a verb is used irrespective of person, number, and gender but to indicate past continuous tense, helping verb “was not” is used for the subjects’ I/He/She and “were not” for the subjects “We/You/They”.

Subject + Tense marker + (object/adverb) +verb (Present Form) + Time (Future)
Ɣän bä wargak lääri̱ kuɛn i̱ruun.
Kɔn bi̱ nɛy wargak lääri̱ kuɛn i̱ruun.
Ji̱n bi̱ wargak lääri̱ kuɛn i̱ruun.
Jɛn bɛ wargak lääri̱ kuɛn i̱ruun.
Yiɛn bia wargak lääri̱ kuɛn i̱ruun.
Kɛn bi̱ kɛn wargak lääri̱ kuɛn i̱ruun.

In the Nuer language, the verb form remains the same regardless of person, number, or gender in the future tense. Only the future-tense marker changes according to the subject: For first-person singular (I), the future-tense marker is “bä”. For third-person singular (he/she), the future-tense marker is “bɛ”. For first-person plural (we), second-person singular (you – male and female), second-person plural (you all), and third-person plural (they), the future-tense marker is “bi̱”.
entries.english: In English Language, “Present form” of a verb is used irrespective of person, number, and gender but to indicate the future tense the helping verb “will/shall” is used before the verb.
